scope: Pricing, credit, quota and removal changes in AI coding tools and the model APIs they bill through.

items.title: GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna list at half the token price of the GPT-5.6 models they replace
items.detail: OpenAI made GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna available on September 22, 2026. On the OpenAI pricing page, standard short-context rates are $2.00 input / $0.20 cached input / $10.00 output per million tokens for GPT-6 Sol, and $0.10 / $0.01 / $0.50 for GPT-6 Luna. The same page still lists their predecessors at $4.00 / $0.40 / $20.00 for GPT-5.6 Sol and $0.20 / $0.02 / $1.20 for GPT-5.6 Luna, so Sol input and output both fall by half and Luna output falls from $1.20 to $0.50. GPT-6 Astra, released earlier, remains at $10.00 / $1.00 / $50.00. Long-context variants are listed at higher rates than the short-context rates quoted here. VentureBeat reported that an OpenAI spokesperson called these permanent prices rather than promotional or introductory pricing. No retirement date was announced for the GPT-5.6 models, which remain listed.
items.impact: Anyone already running GPT-5.6 Sol or Luna workloads can move to the GPT-6 equivalent and pay half the input and output rate, with cached input dropping in the same proportion. The GPT-5.6 models keep working at their current listed rates, so this is an opt-in saving that requires changing the model name in your calls, not an automatic reduction to your existing bill.

items.title: Anthropic raises five-hour usage limits on Pro, Max, Team and seat-based Enterprise plans
items.detail: In the Claude Opus 5.5 announcement on September 22, 2026, Anthropic stated that it is increasing five-hour usage limits on Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise plans, and that subscription users are being given a rate limit reset which can be saved and used at a time of the subscriber choosing. Anthropic published no figures for the size of the increase, no before and after numbers, and no date on which the higher limits take effect. The announcement does not say whether weekly limits change.
items.impact: Subscribers on these plans get more work out of the same monthly fee within each rolling five-hour window, with no action required and no plan change. The saved rate limit reset is a one-off that can be held back and spent on a session that would otherwise be cut short. Because no numbers were published, the increase cannot be budgeted against in advance, so treat current limits as the planning floor until the new figures appear in the usage docs.

items.title: Claude Code switches the default model on Pro and Team Standard plans from Sonnet to Opus
items.detail: Claude Code v2.1.280, released September 22, 2026, changed the default model on Pro and Team Standard plans from Sonnet to Opus, matching the default already used on Max, Team Premium, and Enterprise. The same release made Claude Opus 5.5 the default Opus model. Claude Code documentation states that subscription usage draws on a per-seat allowance over a rolling five-hour window and a weekly window, and describes separate model-family limit messages for Opus and for Sonnet, so work that previously drew on the Sonnet limit now draws on the Opus limit unless the user sets a model with the /model command or a default in /config.
items.impact: Pro and Team Standard subscribers who change nothing now run Opus by default on every new session, at the same subscription price but drawing against a different model limit than before. Anyone who sized their working habits around the Sonnet default should expect a different rate of allowance consumption and can return to the old behaviour by selecting Sonnet in /model or setting a default in /config. Anthropic paired this with an unquantified increase to five-hour limits on the same plans.

items.title: Claude Opus 5.5 launches at $4 / $20 per MTok, 20% below Opus 5
items.detail: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) on September 22, 2026, priced at $4 input / $20 output per million tokens, versus $5 / $25 for Claude Opus 5. Cache reads drop to $0.20 per MTok from $0.50, and 1-hour cache writes fall to $8 from $10. It ships with a 1M token context window by default, 128k max output tokens, and always-on adaptive thinking. Fast mode for Opus 5.5 is priced at $8 / $40 per MTok, versus $10 / $50 for fast mode on Opus 5. Opus 5.5 is available on the Claude API, Claude in Amazon Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Claude on Google Cloud, and Claude in Microsoft Foundry.
items.impact: Anyone already paying Opus 5 rates gets a like-for-like model at a 20% lower list price on both input and output tokens, plus cheaper caching, without switching plans. Existing Opus 5 deployments keep working at the old $5/$25 rate since Opus 5 was not deprecated alongside this launch.

items.title: Vercel AI Gateway cuts Grok 4.7 price 40% for one week
items.detail: Vercel added Grok 4.7 (spacexai/grok-4.7) to AI Gateway on September 21, 2026, with a 40% discount on input and output tokens that applies automatically through September 27. Discounted pricing is $1.20 per million input tokens and $3.60 per million output tokens. The model has a 500K token context window and is reachable through the AI SDK, the OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions API, and coding agents connected to AI Gateway, including fx, Cursor, Codex, Amp, and OpenCode.
items.impact: Anyone routing coding-agent traffic to Grok 4.7 through Vercel AI Gateway pays 40% less per token through September 27, with no code change needed since the discount is automatic. The rate reverts to standard pricing after that date unless Vercel extends it.

items.title: Vercel extended Spend Management budget controls to Enterprise Flexible Commitment plans
items.detail: Spend Management, previously available on Pro, is now included at no additional cost for Enterprise teams on Flexible Commitment plans. Admins can set a budget per billing cycle; when metered usage approaches or crosses it, Spend Management can send email notifications, trigger a webhook, or pause the production deployments of all projects. Setting a budget does not pause usage on its own, and pausing does not stop AI Gateway or v0 usage.
items.impact: If your Enterprise plan is Flexible Commitment rather than a fixed contract, you now have the same opt-in cost-capping tools Pro customers have had. It only pauses project deployments, so a spend spike coming from AI Gateway or v0 keeps billing even with a budget pause enabled.

items.title: GitHub Copilot will drop six more models on October 19, including GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.4
items.detail: Gemini 3.7 Flash, GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4, GPT-5.4 mini, GPT-5 mini and Grok 4.5 are deprecated across all Copilot experiences (Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, code completions) on October 19, 2026. Suggested replacements are Gemini 3.8 Flash, GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-5.6 Luna and Grok 4.6. For Enterprise and Business customers the replacement models are auto-enabled unless an admin has disabled default model enablement.
items.impact: A second Copilot model cutoff inside two months, on GitHub's own schedule rather than the model vendors'. Anything pinned to GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4, GPT-5.4 mini, GPT-5 mini, Gemini 3.7 Flash or Grok 4.5 through the Copilot layer stops resolving on October 19 regardless of that model's status on the vendor's own API.

items.title: GPT-5 and o3 model snapshots are removed from the API on December 11
items.detail: Older GPT-5 and o3 snapshots were given notice of removal from the API. Pinned snapshot IDs do not roll forward to a successor.
items.impact: If you pinned an older snapshot to keep output stable, the call stops resolving on that date rather than silently upgrading. Budget a migration and an eval pass before December.

items.title: The Assistants API was removed; Responses API is the only path
items.detail: Teams on the Assistants API must migrate to the Responses API. Threads, runs and the assistant object have no drop-in equivalent.
items.impact: A rewrite of the orchestration layer, not a model swap. If you have not migrated, this is already broken rather than pending.

items.title: Anthropic cancelled the planned Sonnet 5 price rise and made $2 / $10 permanent
items.detail: An increase to $3 input and $15 output per million tokens had been scheduled for September 1, 2026. Anthropic cancelled it on August 11 and kept the launch rate of $2 input and $10 output.
items.impact: A price rise that was announced and then withdrawn. If you rebudgeted or migrated off Sonnet 5 in anticipation, the reason for that move no longer exists.

items.title: MCP spec now requires 12 months between deprecation and removal
items.detail: The 2026-07-28 revision of the Model Context Protocol specification introduced a formal deprecation policy mandating a minimum twelve-month window between a feature being deprecated and its earliest possible removal.
items.impact: The first enforceable stability guarantee anywhere in this stack. No model API currently offers a window this long, so anything you build against MCP carries less migration risk than the same thing built against a vendor SDK.

items.title: Memory keeps billing while a Fluid function waits on I/O
items.detail: Active CPU billing pauses when a request is blocked on I/O, but provisioned memory billing continues for the full wall-clock duration of the invocation.
items.impact: The headline saving is real but it is CPU-only. An agent that sits for 40 seconds waiting on a model still pays memory for all 40 seconds. Model the memory line separately before assuming the 90 percent figure applies to your bill.

items.title: Replit Agent moved from $0.25 flat checkpoints to effort-based pricing
items.detail: The Agent now prices each task by the time and computation it decides the task required, bundled into a single checkpoint, instead of splitting work into fixed $0.25 checkpoints. Rolled out to new users immediately and reached existing Core and Teams subscribers from July 1, 2026.
items.impact: You cannot see the price before committing to a task, and the cost lands after the run. Users report being billed on runs that hung or errored. Simple edits can land under $0.25; heavy tasks run well above it.

items.title: Vercel Functions on Fluid compute switched to Active CPU pricing
items.detail: CPU is billed at $0.128 per hour only while code is actively executing, with provisioned memory at $0.0106 per GB-hour. A Standard machine at full CPU moves from about $0.31842 per hour to about $0.149 per hour.
items.impact: A genuine decrease for anything that waits on a model call. Long-running agents and LLM inference stop paying full rate while blocked on I/O.

items.title: Cursor rebuilt spend alerting with dollar thresholds routed to Slack or email
items.detail: Admins can set spend thresholds in dollars and route the alerts to Slack or email before the invoice arrives.
items.impact: Turn this on. It is the only mechanism that catches a runaway agent loop inside the billing period rather than after it.

items.title: Cognition renamed Windsurf to Devin Desktop through an over-the-air update
items.detail: Cognition, which acquired Windsurf in 2025, pushed the rename straight to installed clients rather than shipping it as a separate product.
items.impact: The editor you subscribed to changed identity without an opt-in. Worth knowing if you name the product in internal docs, expense claims or procurement records.

items.title: Third-party model requests carry $0.25 per million tokens above the model's own API price
items.detail: On Teams and Enterprise plans, every third-party model request adds $0.25 per million tokens on top of what the model provider charges.
items.impact: A margin layer on top of the provider rate. Check whether bringing your own key avoids it on your plan before assuming it does.

items.title: Copilot replaced Premium Request Units with AI Credits metered on token consumption
items.detail: From June 1, 2026 Copilot plans bill on usage. Premium Request Units are gone and GitHub AI Credits, tied to tokens consumed, took their place. Monthly plans are Pro at $10 including $15 of credits, Pro Plus at $39 including $70, and Max at $100 including $200. Code completions and next-edit suggestions stay unlimited on paid plans, but chat, agents, Copilot CLI, Spaces and Spark all draw down the allowance or bill on top. Annual Pro and Pro Plus customers stay on request-based pricing until their plan expires.
items.impact: A fixed request budget became a variable token bill. The same amount of work now costs different amounts depending on context size, so a large repository is more expensive to work in than a small one at identical effort.

items.title: Copilot code review costs 13 premium requests per review instead of 1
items.detail: From June 1, 2026 Copilot code review carries a model multiplier of 13. Every pull request review, and every code review inside the IDE, takes 13 from the monthly premium request quota. Model multipliers rose across the board on the same date for annual plan holders still on request-based billing.
items.impact: If you wired Copilot review into CI or made it a habit on every pull request, your quota now drains thirteen times faster for that workflow. Developers summarised the change as getting less for the same price. Check whether review is worth 13x against your own quota before leaving it switched on for every PR.

items.title: Bolt raised Pro tokens 30 percent from 10M to 13M with no price increase
items.detail: On May 5, 2026 the Bolt Pro tier went from 10 million to 13 million monthly tokens at the same price. The free plan runs on 1 million tokens per month against a separate daily cap, and sources disagree on whether that daily cap is currently 150K or 300K, so it is not stated here as fact.
items.impact: More headroom for the same money, which is rare enough in this list to be worth noting. Bolt bills by token, so cost still scales with codebase size rather than with how many prompts you send.

items.title: Lovable merged its two balances into one credit pool and complex generations now cost 2 to 3 credits
items.detail: Hosting and AI were previously billed as two separate balances. A single unified credit pool now covers building, hosting, backend and the AI features inside the deployed app. Plan mode stays flat at 1 credit per message while Build mode is usage based, and multi-file generations that used to cost 1 credit now cost 2 to 3. Credit allocations on Starter and Pro were raised in the same period. Sources place all of this in May 2026 without publishing an exact day.
items.impact: The headline allocation went up, but so did the cost of the messages that actually do work. Count credits per completed feature rather than per message when comparing against your old bill.

items.title: Claude Haiku 3 retired and the default replacement costs four times as much
items.detail: Haiku 3 ran at $0.25 input and $1.25 output per million tokens. The migration path is Haiku 4.5 at $1 and $5, or Haiku 3.5 at $0.80 and $4 where cost matters more than capability. Claude Sonnet 3.7 is deprecated as well.
items.impact: A removal that is really a price rise. High-volume classification or extraction built on Haiku 3 economics gets four times more expensive on the default path. Price Haiku 3.5 before defaulting to 4.5.

items.title: Gemini Pro models left the free API tier and now require billing
items.detail: Gemini 3.1 Pro, Gemini 3 Pro and Gemini 2.5 Pro all require a billing account from April 1, 2026. Flash and Flash-Lite stay free on tightened daily quotas, reported at 5 to 15 requests per minute and up to 1,000 requests per day. Sources also describe a free-tier quota cut of 50 to 80 percent from December 2025, and a mandatory monthly spending cap that pauses the API once reached.
items.impact: Any prototype or side project running on free Pro access stopped working that day unless billing was attached. Check whether a Flash model covers the job before paying for Pro.

items.title: Windsurf replaced monthly credits with daily and weekly quotas and moved Pro from $15 to $20
items.detail: Pro previously carried a pool of 500 credits per month. The new plans meter usage as daily and weekly quotas that refresh on their own, with no monthly pool to exhaust. Five tiers now exist: Free, Pro at $20 per month, Max at $200, Teams at $40 per user and Enterprise. Existing paid subscribers keep their old pricing.
items.impact: A quota is a rate limit, not a budget. You can no longer spend a whole month of allowance on one large project in a single week, however much is notionally left. If your work is bursty, that constraint bites harder than the price rise.

items.title: GitHub deprecated selected Anthropic and OpenAI models inside Copilot
items.detail: Model availability was withdrawn at the Copilot layer, on GitHub's own schedule rather than the model vendors'.
items.impact: Two deprecation calendars apply to you, not one. A model can stay live on the vendor API while the tool you reach it through drops it.

items.title: v0 moved from fixed message counts to metering actual input and output tokens
items.detail: v0 previously charged a fixed number of credits per message. It now meters the real input and output tokens each generation consumes and converts those to credits, so longer prompts, attachments, source files and larger outputs all cost more. Sources place the switch in February 2026 without publishing an exact day, so this entry is dated to the start of that month.
items.impact: Cost now scales with how big your project is, not how many times you ask. The same request against a large codebase costs more than against a small one, which makes credit burn accelerate as a project grows rather than staying flat.

items.title: Cursor apologised and refunded users after an unannounced Pro plan limit change
items.detail: A change to the $20/month Pro plan produced unexpected charges. Anysphere's CEO acknowledged the communication was unclear, rolled back the limits and refunded affected users.
items.impact: The precedent worth remembering: allowance changes on this tier have shipped without notice before, and the correction came only after public pressure.
